key_insight: A learned latent-dynamics module captures history-dependent deformations (e.g., loose clothing, hair, contacts) and integrates with pose-driven neural rendering, producing temporally coherent full-body avatar animation without requiring explicit garment templates.
problem_solved: Pose-only avatar models cannot predict motion-dependent states because the same pose can correspond to many different dynamic configurations; explicit garment simulation needs templates that raw multi-view capture typically doesn't provide. This work models those dynamics directly from captured data.
method: Factor pose vs. dynamic residuals: represent per-frame non-rigid, history-dependent state as a compact latent code that complements skeletal pose.

Learn a temporal latent-dynamics model (e.g., RNN/transformer-style transition) that predicts latent evolution from prior latent + current pose, then feed pose + latent to a neural renderer (NeRF/texture-based) to synthesize views.

Train end-to-end from multi-view video using reconstruction and temporal-consistency losses (optionally contact/inertia priors), eliminating the need for explicit garment templates or manual layering.
impact: Delivers more realistic, temporally coherent avatar animations from raw capture with less manual setup, benefiting virtual production, telepresence, games, and any application needing believable human motion without costly garment modeling.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pose input → latent-dynamics module (temporal loop) → neural renderer → rendered frames
Before/after comparison: pose-only rendering vs. pose+latent rendering showing improved cloth/hair dynamics
Latent trajectory visualization: 2D/3D plot of latent state evolution for a motion sequence (showing different responses for same pose depending on history)
Optional schematic: contact/inertia effects (arrows) illustrating why dynamics depend on history, not just instantaneous pose
paper_title: Latent Dynamics for Full Body Avatar Animation
paper_authors: Shichong Peng, Chengxiang Yin, Fei Jiang, Zhongshi Jiang, Lingchen Yang
